offence_severity: Death (Section 302) - Minimum 10 years, Maximum Life Imprisonment or Death
physical_harm: The deceased died as a result of the gunshot wound. Others were injured, including the mother of the deceased and the son of the deceased.
premeditation_planning: Yes, the court found a pre-arranged plan and prior meeting of minds among the accused
motive: To teach a lesson for the deceased's refusal to reap their crop
key_evidence_accepted: The prosecution witnesses' testimony, including Baburam P.W. 6 and Satyanarain P.W. 7, was accepted as consistent and credible, establishing the sequence of events leading to the deceased's death.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, despite grueling cross-examination, and found their testimony consistent and reliable.

legal_representation.accused: D.B. Vohra, T. Hashmi, S.K. Sabharwal

appeal_history.trial_court: Conviction under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant, along with his father and brother, went to the house of the deceased with weapons, engaged in a verbal altercation, and that the brother of the appellant, on exhortation of his father, fired at the deceased, resulting in his death. The prosecution contended that the appellant was rightly convicted under sections 302 and 34 of the IPC due to the prearranged plan and common intention among the accused.
defence_argument: The appellant contended that in the facts and circumstances of the case, Section 34 IPC could not be invoked, arguing that there was no direct evidence of a common intention or prearranged plan among the accused.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle of vicarious or constructive liability under Section 34 IPC, emphasizing the need for a common intention and actual participation in the commission of the crime, which may develop on the spot but must be anterior in point of time to the commission of the crime.
precedent_relied_upon: Barendra Kumar Ghosh v. King Emperor AIR 1925 PC 1; Mehbub Shah v. King-Emperor AIR 1945 PC 148; Pandurang, Tukia and Bhillia v. The State of Hyderabad (1955) 1 SCR 1083; Mohan Singh & Anr. v. State of Punjab AIR 1963 SC 174; State of UP v. Itikhar Khan & Ors. (1973) 1 SCC 512; Ramaswami Ayyangar & Others v. State of Tamil Nadu (1976) 3 SCC 779; Rambilas Singh & Ors. v. State of Bihar (1989) 3 SCC 605; Krishnan & Another v. State of Kerala (1996) 10 SCC 508; Surendra Chauhan v. State of MP (2000) 4 SCC 110; Suresh & Another v. State of UP (2001) 3 SCC 673; Gopi Nath @ Jha//ar v. State of UP (2001) 6 SCC 620; Krishnan & Anr. v. State represented by Inspector of Police (2003) 7 SCC 56; Girija Shankar v. State of UP (2004) 3 SCC 793; Ramesh Singh @ Photti v. State of A.P. (2004) 11 sec 305
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the appellant, along with his father and brother, had a prearranged plan and common intention to teach the deceased a lesson, and the appellant was found to be vicariously liable for the act of his brother who shot the deceased.
